people.died_place: No. 30 General Hospital, near Boulogne, France

occupations.employer: 2nd North Midland Field Company, Royal Engineers
occupations.notes: Volunteered on the outbreak of war and was gazetted Second Lieutenant in September 1914; Lieutenant, then Captain in December 1915, Major in June 1916. Served in France and Flanders from February 1915, was severely wounded and invalided home that April, rejoined in November 1916, and in 1917 was second in command at a base park near Calais. Died of pneumonia, probably after influenza, on 26 January 1919; buried at Les Baraques Military Cemetery, Sangatte. Remembered at St Thomas's and St Mary's churches in Nottingham, on the Notts Amateur Cricket Club and Nottinghamshire Freemasons war memorials, and on the family headstone in the Church (Rock) Cemetery.

people.bio:
Solicitor, head of Maples and McCraith of the Pavement, Nottingham — the firm he founded with Samuel Maples, to whom he had been articled — and a founder member of the Nottingham Incorporated Law Society, its president in 1891. A Justice of the Peace from 1892, he was knighted in January 1918. He was Chairman of the Nottingham Central Conservative Association, and a director of the Coliseum Syndicate Ltd and of St Augustine's Parade Hippodrome, Bristol, Ltd.

He married Maria Elizabeth Dickinson in 1876. In 1911 he signed the census schedule for Ellenborough House but was not at home on census night, which is why his wife is returned as head of the household and he has no 1911 record. In 1921 the household was on Clumber Crescent South, but by his death he was back at Ellenborough House, 3 South Road, where the family had lived since at least 1891. He died there on 9 July 1928, aged 75, leaving a gross estate of £151,442, with net personalty of £149,624. His second son, Major Bernard McCraith, had died on active service in 1919.
